rv.q: Zimmerman crafts a show that while lovely to behold, too often treats the words like an afterthought.
Not many plays can provide solid and varied entertainment and be potentially life-altering at the same time, but this is one of them.
It's a tight, compact 90-minutes of real genius shared with an audience, both from its subject and its author.
For a genuinely remarkable theatrical experience, Mary Zimmerman's scholarly and artistic masterpiece is well worth a visit.
There is no other playwright-director, alive or dead, like Mary Zimmerman. She creates work that only her mind is capable of.

Reciting his encyclopedic works on stage does not necessarily lend itself to curiosity on our part; it does lend itself to boredom.
